claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition, 2026 Valentine's Day SKU launch) asserts that seasonal holiday SKUs require precise inventory ordering calibrated to sell out by the holiday date, because unsold units have near-zero residual value after the holiday window — no retailer or consumer wants a Valentine's Day product in March or April. Over-ordering creates write-off risk; under-ordering caps revenue. The constraint is binary in a way that evergreen SKUs are not.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: Limited-edition seasonal SKU tied to a specific holiday (Valentine's Day)
Physical consumer product with branded holiday packaging
claims.mechanism: Holiday-themed packaging loses relevance immediately after the event, eliminating sell-through and resale value, which means every unit above demand is a sunk cost.
bounded_by: Does not apply to evergreen SKUs or flavors sold year-round without holiday branding

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition, 2026 launch planning) states that when retail partner distribution calendars are fully committed for the year, a new product must launch exclusively through direct digital channels — specifically Amazon and TikTok Shop — rather than waiting for the next retail cycle. The retail calendar acts as a hard constraint that determines channel routing for time-sensitive launches.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: New flavor or SKU ready for launch mid-cycle
Retail partner annual product calendars already finalized
Time-sensitive launch window (e.g., Valentine's Day) cannot be deferred to next retail cycle
claims.mechanism: Retail partner planograms and purchase orders are committed annually; introducing an unplanned SKU mid-cycle is operationally infeasible, so digital-first channels (Amazon, TikTok Shop) absorb the launch capacity.
bounded_by: Does not apply when retail partners have flex slots or when the launch is not time-sensitive

claims.text: Greg LaVecchia (Bloom Nutrition) asserts that in-person community events with existing customers serve as high-signal product research — in this case, a live tasting at a Bloom community event identified Strawberry Rose as the community's top flavor preference, which directly drove the decision to launch it as the next SKU. Real-world community preference outweighed internal product development intuition.
claims.speaker: Greg LaVecchia
conditions: Brand with an active community that participates in in-person events
Product development in a category with subjective preference (taste, flavor)
claims.mechanism: Direct preference feedback from engaged brand community members eliminates the guessing inherent in internal flavor development decisions, aligning the product roadmap with demonstrated customer desire.
bounded_by: Requires an existing engaged community willing to attend in-person events
Most applicable to taste-driven or preference-driven consumer products

examples.text: Bloom Nutrition (Greg LaVecchia, 2026) planned to launch the Strawberry Rose flavor of their supplement drink after it ranked as the top preference among Bloom community members at a live in-person tasting event. Because the 2026 retail partner calendar was already locked, the launch was routed exclusively to Amazon and TikTok Shop as a Valentine's Day seasonal SKU. The creative team developed holiday-specific packaging (individual cans personalized with messages like 'Mine to Mari from Greg') to make it giftable. LaVecchia publicly acknowledged the inventory risk: selling out by February 14th was the target, because any remaining inventory post-Valentine's Day would be unsellable at full value. Influencers Jen and Val — dance-platform stars who were already organic Bloom fans — were signed as the campaign's lead faces, framing the partnership as authentic fit rather than paid placement.

practices.text: When selecting influencer partners for a campaign, prioritize creators who already use and love the product organically before the partnership begins; authentic product affinity produces more credible content and reduces the risk of audience skepticism about paid endorsement.

For seasonal holiday SKUs, set the inventory order target at the quantity you can sell through by the holiday date, not the maximum you could sell if demand were unlimited; the post-holiday residual value of holiday-branded packaging is near zero.

When retail partner calendars block a new SKU for the current year, use Amazon and TikTok Shop as the primary launch channels to capture the time-sensitive window rather than waiting for the next retail cycle.
